You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer driver-run):
- file: driver/plan.hpp:35
- category: stale-doc
- title: Step::engine_id comment shows ids ('qemu', 'verilator:...') that no longer exist
- detail: plan.hpp:35 annotates engine_id with `// "qemu" | "verilator:ax45mpv_premium"`. Real ids are 'qemu64'/'qemu32' (engine_registry.hpp:30-31 kQemuId64/kQemuId32; cmd_run.cpp:555 builds Step{kQemuId64, ...}) and 'vsim:<cfg>' - normalize_engine_label (engine_registry.hpp:61-64) rewrites 'verilator:<cfg>' to 'vsim:<cfg>' before any id is used, with the explicit contract that 'a user never sees verilator'. Both example ids in the comment would fail find_engine lookups today.
- claimed safety: Comment-only change.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.

in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a

optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,

1	// The phase-plan grammar driven by run_plan (F6), minus the dropped QEMU2
2	// step.
3	//
4	// A Plan is a list of Steps; each Step names an engine (by id, resolved against
5	// the F2 registry), the role to invoke it in (its `invoke` template key, e.g.
6	// "fast-leg" / "accurate-leg"), and a Trigger. run_plan spawns each leg in
7	// order, threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward, and returns each
8	// leg's mcycle/minstret. Under the no-QEMU2-handback design every F6 step
9	// drains, so the hybrid cycle figure is the vsim-leg mcycle minus the qemu-leg
10	// mcycle.
11	#ifndef ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
12	#define ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
13	
14	#include <map>
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
19	
20	namespace andes_sim {
21	
22	// The ROI delimiter for a step. `kind` is marker|pc; `params` carries
23	// kind-specific values (e.g. enter_pc, exit_pc) that F9 maps onto trigger
24	// args. F6 only exercises the default marker case (no params).
25	struct Trigger {
26	  std::string kind;
27	  std::map<std::string, std::string> params;
28	};
29	
30	// One leg of a plan: which engine, which invoke role, under which trigger.
31	// `extra_args` are verbatim tokens appended after the filled template and the
32	// trigger args -- the seam for user-forwarded per-leg flags (e.g. the vsim
33	// leg's --kanata), which are orthogonal to the trigger.
34	struct Step {
35	  std::string engine_id;  // "qemu" | "verilator:ax45mpv_premium"
36	  std::string role;       // invoke-template key: "fast-leg" | "accurate-leg"
37	  Trigger trigger;
38	  std::vector<std::string> extra_args{};  // default-init: keeps 3-field Step{} literals warning-free
39	};
40	
41	// A whole hybrid run. Every step loads `elf`; the shared mmap (`mem_size`
42	// bytes, at `mmap_path` or allocated by run_plan when empty) survives across
43	// every leg so memory threads through.
44	struct Plan {
45	  std::string elf;          // path to the ELF every leg launches
46	  long long mem_size = 0;   // shared-mmap size in bytes
47	  std::string mmap_path;    // "" => run_plan allocates one (F5) and owns it
48	  std::vector<Step> steps;
49	  // The engine whose hardware the fast leg(s) must model when the plan has
50	  // NO accurate-leg step of its own (the --verify oracle plan): the ISA sync
51	  // ({vlen}, {qemu_cpu}, -readconfig, LM sidecars) reads this engine instead.
52	  // Empty => derive from the plan's accurate-leg step (the normal case).
53	  std::string hw_engine_id;
54	};
55	
56	// What one drain step measured (read back from its state file), plus the
57	// leg's captured stdout -- the guest program's own output (UART/semihosting)
58	// rides the engine's stdout and must flow through to the user. `st` is the
59	// full drained record (verify_oracle F4: run --verify diffs the vsim drain
60	// against the oracle leg's in-process, after run_plan removed the files).
61	struct PhaseResult {
62	  unsigned long long mcycle = 0;
63	  unsigned long long minstret = 0;
64	  std::string out;
65	  hybrid_state_v1 st{};
66	};
67	
68	// Aggregate outcome. `error` empty => every step matched its expected exit and
69	// drained a valid state file; `phases` then holds one entry per step in order.
70	struct PlanResult {
71	  std::string error;
72	  std::vector<PhaseResult> phases;
73	  // The concrete per-step argv run_plan built (after placeholder fill, qemu_cfg
74	  // staging, and state threading). Populated whether or not the steps spawn, so
75	  // a --dry-run can print the exact commands without executing them.
76	  std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> argvs;
77	  // On a leg failure: where the kept evidence lives (the workdir's drain/
78	  // sidecar/cfg files, a copy of the ELF, manifest.txt). Empty on success or
79	  // when the bundle could not be written.
80	  std::string repro_dir;
81	  bool ok() const { return error.empty(); }
82	};
83	
84	}  // namespace andes_sim
85	
86	#endif  // ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP

input.reason: Verified: plan.hpp:35 annotates Step::engine_id with example ids "qemu" and "verilator:ax45mpv_premium", neither of which exists in the production registry. builtin_qemu_arch (engine_registry.cpp) registers only kQemuId64="qemu64"/kQemuId32="qemu32" (engine_registry.hpp:30-31), cmd_run.cpp:555 builds Step{kQemuId64,...}, and normalize_engine_label (engine_registry.hpp:61-64, applied at engine_registry.cpp:171 before dedup) rewrites verilator:<cfg> to vsim:<cfg> so no downstream consumer ever sees "verilator:". find_engine (run_plan.cpp:93) is an exact id match, so both example ids would fail lookup today. Refutation checks: unit tests using id "qemu" register their own fake descriptors (unaffected by a comment edit); no test, script, or cross-repo consumer references the comment text. Fixing the comment is behavior-free. Note: engine_descriptor.hpp:26 carries the same stale example ids and could be fixed in the same pass.
